title: Request bodies that spell one protobuf field both snake_case and camelCase are rejected
answers: 400 'Request specifies both secret_id and secretId' on a gateway API call
protobuf JSON body with both snake_case and camelCase keys for the same field
gateway secret update authorized against one secret but applied to another via camelCase key
conflicting duplicate field names in MLflow REST request JSON
body:
Symptom: a gateway secret or model-definition request whose JSON carries both `secret_id` and `secretId` (or both `model_configs` and `modelConfigs`) is authorized against one id but the handler acts on the other, because the later key wins.
Root cause: mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_request_message ran parse_dict, which accepts both proto and JSON names, while basic-auth validators read the raw snake_case key from the Flask body.
Fix pattern: call mlflow/server/handlers.py:_reject_conflicting_field_aliases on the normalized JSON before parse_dict. It checks each field's name and json_name, recurses into nested message fields (lists included), and raises INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE "Request specifies both 'x' and 'y'".
Constraints: map fields and google.protobuf well-known types are skipped because their keys are caller-chosen. _get_workspace_request_message calls parse_dict itself, so any new direct parse_dict of a request body in handlers.py must run the same check.
Applies: every protobuf-backed request body parsed in mlflow/server/handlers.py, not only gateway routes.
applies: Server-side request parsing in mlflow/server/handlers.py for any proto-backed endpoint.
says: Gateway secret update modifies a different secret than the authorized identifier.
API requests with mixed naming conventions cause unexpected parameter overrides.
Reject API payloads that provide conflicting aliases for the same configuration setting.
Server returns a bad request error when both casing styles are submitted.
search: Server request parsing in mlflow/server/handlers.py must reject JSON bodies that define conflicting snake_case and camelCase field aliases before calling parse_dict. The helper mlflow/server/handlers.py:_reject_conflicting_field_aliases checks field names and json_name across nested messages and lists, raising INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE when duplicates appear. Map fields and google.protobuf well-known types are excluded, and direct parse_dict calls in _get_workspace_request_message must also enforce this check across all protobuf-backed endpoints.
